Package org.apache.juneau.console.freemarker

Class DatatablesCardType

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.console.freemarker.DatatablesCardType
All Implemented Interfaces:
CardTypeHandler
public final class DatatablesCardType extends Object implements CardTypeHandler
The built-in datatables card type, registered through META-INF/services: validates the author catalog and resolves per-column search metadata, with no shape lift — the catalog stays in author shape (key/label, not VIEW_META's data/title); NS.card.liftCatalog (juneau-views.js) does the lift at mount time.
Example:

CardSource s = CardSource.create("datatables", "releases") .body("{dataUrl:'/rest/releases/data', columns:[{key:'version', label:'Version', searchType:'text'}]}") .build(); JsonMap frag = new DatatablesCardType().toFragment(s); // {"table": {...}}

Since:
10.0.0

    • implicitTopics

      public List<String> implicitTopics(JsonMap card)
      filter: and redraw: always; selection:, detail: and bulk: only when the catalog sets that key. A src-only card's catalog arrives at runtime, so it is credited with all five. The JS side applies this same rule and does not re-check once the catalog is known: a topic the catalog turns out not to need stays claimed and is simply never published.
      Specified by:
      implicitTopics in interface CardTypeHandler
      Parameters:
      card - The card object from the page contract (base keys plus this type's fragment).
      Returns:
      The concrete topics (or ns.name:* patterns) the type's JS publishes for this card.

    • acceptedOps

      public Set<String> acceptedOps()
      Description copied from interface: CardTypeHandler
      cmd:<id> ops this type handles, beyond the shell's refresh, for E-43 on a ribbon target. null (the default) means "unknown to Java": the Java validator skips the check and the JS shell reports an unhandled op at runtime (E-JS-48).
      Example:

      @Override public Set<String> acceptedOps() { return Set.of("set-target"); }

      Specified by:
      acceptedOps in interface CardTypeHandler
      Returns:
      The handled op names, or null if unknown.
